title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(k), and ν ≥ 1 is an integer. Grothendieck considers the category C_ν of artinian local rings Λ with residue field k whose maximal ideal m_Λ carries divided powers that are ν-nilpotent. Here this concretely means γ_{p^ν}(x)^p = 0 for x in m_Λ. The divided powers are not required to be compatible with the canonical divided powers of p. He proposes to build an initial object of C_ν.

Argument.
(1) Each Λ is canonically a W-algebra, since W is the Cohen ring of the perfect field k. The image of λ_0 = p lies in m_Λ.
(2) Divided powers on a Z_(p)-algebra are determined by the γ_{p^i}, because primes ℓ ≠ p are invertible (the NB on the page). So everything is governed by the elements Λ_i = γ_{p^i}(Λ_0). These satisfy Λ_i^p = ((p^{i+1})!/(p^i!)^p) Λ_{i+1}, and ν-nilpotence gives Λ_ν^p = 0.
(3) Hence Λ receives a map from
 W^{(ν)} = W[Λ_0,…,Λ_ν] / (Λ_0^p − p!Λ_1, …, Λ_{ν−1}^p − (p^ν)!/((p^{ν−1})!)^p Λ_ν, Λ_ν^p, Λ_0 − pλ_0).
 The final generator is written 'Λ_0 − pλ_0' on the page, but Λ_0 − λ_0 is meant (see errors).
(4) W^{(ν)} is claimed to be universal among W-algebras with a ν-nilpotent PD ideal containing the image of p. Grothendieck announces that it is artinian with maximal ideal J = (Λ_0,…,Λ_ν) and residue field k.

Computation. He first drops the relation Λ_0 = p and works with A^{(ν)}. He writes Λ_i = λ_i + Θ_i, where λ_r = p^{p^r}/(p^r)! = γ_{p^r}(p) is the 'usual' value in W. The next page shows:
- A^{(ν)} is W-free on the monomials Θ^a with 0 ≤ a_i ≤ p−1.
- A Lemma describes the ideal I = (Θ_0): Θ_i is p^i-torsion modulo I, and p^{c(ν)} ∈ I, with c(ν) = ν + p[p^ν − (p^{ν−1}+…+1)].

So W^{(ν)} is W/p^{c(ν)} plus a torsion part spanned by the Θ-monomials. The Θ_i measure how far γ_{p^i}(p) can deviate from p^{p^i}/(p^i)! when no compatibility with the canonical PD of p is imposed.

Check for ν = 1: Θ_1 is killed by p. From Λ_1^p = 0 one gets λ_1^p + Θ_1^p = 0. Multiplying by p gives p^{1+p(p−1)} = 0, consistent with c(1) = 1 + p(p−1).

In modern terms, W^{(ν)} is the ν-nilpotent truncation of the divided-power envelope of (W, pW) over the base (Z_p, (0)), with no compatibility with the canonical divided powers of p. Equivalently it is W⟨x⟩/(x − p, nilpotence). Spec W^{(ν)} is the final object among artinian nilpotent-PD thickenings of Spec k, as needed for Grothendieck's early nilpotent-PD crystalline site (IHES 1966, Dix exposés 1968).

The page sits in a folder of crystalline notes. The preceding page, a Serre–Tate text on Grössencharaktere, is unrelated.
errors: The last relation is written 'Λ_0 − pλ_0'. It must be Λ_0 − λ_0 (λ_0 = p), as the page itself says later ('on omet la relation Λ_0 − λ_0').

Universality is asserted, not proved. Showing that W^{(ν)} actually carries divided powers on J needs an argument: the ideal (Λ_0 − p) is not a priori a sub-PD ideal of the free PD algebra. This is Berthelot's general theorem on PD envelopes. The page gives no justification, though the claim is true.

'ν-nilpotent' is encoded only as Λ_ν^p = 0. Whether this matches the definition of ν-PD-nilpotence used elsewhere (e.g. the vanishing of the ν+1-st divided-power filtration step J^{[ν+1]}) is not addressed on this page.
The claimed formula c(ν) = ν + p[p^ν − (p^ν−1)/(p−1)] is checked for ν = 1 in the reconstruction. For general ν it rests on the next page's lemma; the necessity direction is not shown here.

ideas.what: Initial object of the category of artinian local rings with residue field k and ν-nilpotent divided powers on the maximal ideal (with no compatibility with p).
ideas.modern_name: (Truncated) divided-power envelope of (W(k), pW) over (Z_p, 0); final object of the nilpotent crystalline site of Spec k among artinian thickenings
ideas.usually_credited_to: PD envelopes in general: Berthelot (thesis, 1974; Berthelot–Ogus 1978). Nilpotent PD crystalline setting: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1966/68).
ideas.where_published: Closest: Grothendieck, Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, in Dix exposés (1968), which uses nilpotent divided powers. The explicit construction of W^{(ν)} is not known to appear there.

ideas.what: Divided powers in a Z_(p)-algebra are generated by γ_{p^i}, with Λ_i^p = ((p^{i+1})!/(p^i!)^p) Λ_{i+1}. This gives a presentation of the free PD algebra.
ideas.modern_name: Standard presentation of the PD polynomial algebra Z_(p)⟨x⟩

ideas.what: Writing γ_{p^i}(p) = p^{p^i}/(p^i)! + Θ_i and showing Θ_i is p^i-torsion, with explicit torsion exponent c(ν) for the constants.
ideas.modern_name: p-torsion in the PD envelope of pZ_p when the PD is not compatible with the canonical PD of p
ideas.usually_credited_to: The qualitative phenomenon is a standard example (Berthelot, Berthelot–Ogus notes); explicit nilpotent truncations are not standardly credited.

missed.claim: Grothendieck gives an explicit structure theorem for the universal artinian ν-nilpotent PD thickening of a perfect field k. It is W(k)/p^{c(ν)} plus a torsion module spanned by monomials in Θ_i = γ_{p^i}(p) − p^{p^i}/(p^i)!, with c(ν) = ν + p[p^ν − (p^{ν−1}+…+1)]. This quantifies the failure of the 'naive' crystalline site, without compatibility with the canonical PD of p, and appears to be the computation motivating the later insistence on compatibility with (W, pW, γ) as base.
missed.quote: On va construire un objet initial de cette catégorie ... W^{(ν)} = W[Λ_0, …, Λ_ν]/(Λ_0^p − p!Λ_1, …, Λ_ν^p; Λ_0 − λ_0) ... universel
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical witness of why Berthelot's crystalline theory takes the PD base (W, pW) with its canonical divided powers. It also gives an explicit example of torsion in PD envelopes, which is relevant to prismatic and absolute crystalline comparisons (e.g. the crystalline site over Z_p versus over W).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful explicit computation of a universal nilpotent PD thickening. The torsion phenomenon is known in principle, but the explicit exponent c(ν) and the Θ-basis are an unpublished detail, and the computation is a historically informative precursor to the choice of PD base in crystalline cohomology. It is not a new theorem.
